newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU must harness social policy, competition - Kok.
newsitem.headline: EU must harness social policy, competition - Kok.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday that European Union social policy must be harnessed to competitiveness to create more jobs in the 15-nation bloc.

"By utilising this interaction (between competitiveness and social policies) we shall be able to create a stronger basis for employment and prosperity in a caring and supportive society," Kok told a conference in the Dutch capital.
Kok's Labour-led coalition currently holds the six-month presidency of the EU, which is grappling with an average 11 percent unemployment.
He said Europe had performed less well than other major global players such as Japan and the United States in creating new jobs over the last decade.
"During that time, (EU) employment has risen by only four percent, as opposed to nine percent in Japan and 17 percent in the USA," Kok said.
As such, measures to boost the EU's competitive position and create more jobs amounted to "social policy, pure and simple", he said.

But he cautioned that the EU had to maintain a minimum level of social provision -- "Inadequate social policy may yield results in the short term...by cutting costs. In the long term, however, it will have an adverse effect on a country's competitiveness."
Social policy provided necessary security in an increasingly flexible and turbulent labour market, Kok added.
